result.summary: The image shows a signalized intersection with a high-visibility continental crosswalk and sidewalks on both sides. While basic infrastructure is present, the wide crossing distance and lack of a refuge island or curb extensions increase pedestrian exposure to vehicle traffic.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a median or refuge island, increasing exposure time.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground, the continental crosswalk across the main road.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signal Visibility
hazards.description: While traffic lights are present, dedicated pedestrian signal heads are not clearly visible from this angle, which may lead to confusion about when it is safe to cross.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signal to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before vehicles get a green light, increasing visibility.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised island in the center of the roadway to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

result.summary: The image shows an urban intersection with basic pedestrian infrastructure including sidewalks and a marked crosswalk. However, the environment is degraded by poor pavement quality, lack of ADA-compliant curb ramps, and significant visual obstructions from parked vehicles near the crossing.

hazards.name: Daylighting Obstruction
hazards.description: Vehicles parked immediately adjacent to the crosswalk on the left side of the image block sight lines between drivers and pedestrians entering the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street, parked silver car near the intersection.

hazards.name: Lack of ADA Accessibility
hazards.description: The curb at the crosswalk lacks a ramp, creating a trip hazard and a barrier for people with mobility devices.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground right, where the sidewalk meets the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Pavement Degradation
hazards.description: The roadway surface is cracked and uneven, which can cause tripping or affect vehicle braking performance.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground and throughout the intersection.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to shorten the crossing distance and prevent illegal parking near the crosswalk, improving visibility.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install detectable warning surfaces and sloped ramps at all crossing points to ensure accessibility.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Upgrade the standard transverse markings to continental or ladder-style markings for better visibility to approaching drivers.
